(b) The mass number of an element is the sum of a total number of protons and neutrons inside in its nucleus and represents by A. Therefore, mass number A= number of protons + number of neutrons. Physical and Chemical Changes, Solution Notes x Matter is deﬁ ned as anything that occupies space and exhibits rest mass or inertia. x The three commonly occurring states of matter include solid, liquid and gas. x In our daily life, we encounter many changes in our surroundings, though we do not notice them, such as souring of milk, rusting of iron, stretching of a rubber band, bread becoming toast, melting of wax, etc. x All these changes that take place around us are either a physical change or chemical change. Physical Changes x Physical changes, are the changes that change the physical traits of the substance, without making any change in their internal structure. x In physical changes no chemical bonds are broken or formed. x Some examples of physical changes are : (i) Melting of wax (ii) Melting of ice (iii) Freezing of water (iv) Vaporization of water (v) Dissolving sugar in water (vi) Chopping in wood (vii) Crumpling of paper x Physical change is a reversible process. Chemical Changes x A chemical change is deﬁ ned as the process in which the atoms of one or more substances are rearranged or combine to form a new substance. x When a substance undergoes a chemical change, the chemical properties of the substance changes and it is transformed into a different substance with different chemical composition. x Energy change is one of the characteristics of a chemical change, because of the formation of a new product. x Once the chemical change takes place, it cannot be reversed. x Some examples of chemical changes are as follows - (i) Adding vinegar to baking soda (ii) Bleaching a stain Join − https://t.me/thehindu000 General Science General Studies G–257 x The molecules of the solvent work to put the solute molecules apart. x Eventually, the molecules of solute become eventually distributed in throughout the solvent. Gaseous Solution : x If the solvent is gas, only gases are dissolved under a given set of conditions. x Example of a gaseous solution is air (Oxygen and other gases dissolved in Nitrogen). 2. Liquid Solution : x If the solvent is a liquid, then almost all gases, liquids and solids can be dissolved. x Examples of liquid solutions are as follows- (i) Gas in liquid - Oxygen in water. (ii) Liquid in liquid - Alcoholic beverages are basically solutions of ethanol in water. (iii) Solid in liquid- Sucrose in water; Sodium chloride in water. 3. Solid solutions : x If the solvent is solid, then gas, liquid and solid can be dissolved. (i) Gas in Solid - Hydrogen dissolves in palladium, this is studied as a means of hydrogen storage. (ii) Liquid in solid - Mercury in gold forming amalgam; Hexane in paraﬃ n wax. (iii) Solid in solid - Alloys like bronze is a solution of copper and zinc. Dilute Solution : x A dilute solution in chemistry is a solution that can accept more solute, until it becomes saturated, or in which there is a relatively small amount of solute dissolved in the solution. Concentrated Solution : x The concentrated solution is a solution that contains a large amount of solute relative to the amount that could dissolve. Saturated solution : x A saturated solution is a solution that can not dissolve any more of the substance that’s been mixed into it. Solubility : x Amount of a substance (called the solute) that dissolves in a unit volume of a liquid substance (called the solvent) to form a saturated solution under speciﬁ ed conditions of temperature and pressure. x Solubility is expressed usually as moles of solute per 100 grams of solvent. (d) Physical changes aﬀ ect the form of a chemical substance, but not its chemical composition. Which of the following is/are the example/examples of chemical change? 1. Crystallization of sodium chloride 2. Melting of ice 3. Souring of milk Select the correct answer using the code given below. (a) 1 and 2 only (b) 3 only (c) 1, 2 and 3 (d) None I.A.S. (Pre) 2014 Ans. (b) A chemical change is a change in which something new is formed (irreversible). The starting materials change into an entirely diﬀ erent substance or substances. This new substance has a diﬀ erent chemical composition than the starting materials. Examples of chemical change would be the reaction of iron with air (rusting) or the reaction of a metal and acid. The crystallization of sodium chloride and melting of ice, both are the examples of a physical change while souring of milk is an example of chemical change. 5. Assertion (A) : A chemical reaction becomes faster at a higher temperature. Reason (R) : At higher temperature, molecular motion becomes more rapid. (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A). (c) (A) is true but (R) is false. (d) (A) is false but (R) is true. I.A.S. (Pre) 2001 Ans. (a) A chemical reaction generally becomes faster at a higher temperature because at higher temperature, molecular motion becomes more rapid and the molecules have higher kinetic energy. The process of a chemical reaction depends on the concentration, temperature and physical state of molecules and their nature. Pasteurization is a process by which – (a) Milk is preserved at a very low temperature for 24 hours (b) Milk is heated for 8 hours (c) First milk is heated up to a longer time and then cooled suddenly within speciﬁ ed time (d) None of these 38th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1992 Ans. (c) In order to pasteurize milk, ﬁ rst, the milk is heated up to a longer time and then cooled suddenly within speciﬁ ed time. Pasteurization is a process invented by French scientist Louis Pasteur during the nineteenth century. In 1864, Louis Pasteur discovered that heating beer and wine was enough to kill most of the bacteria that caused spoilage and hence, prevented these beverages from turning sour. This was achieved by eliminating pathogenic microbes and lowering microbial numbers to prolong the quality of the beverage. 8. Pasteurization is related to : (a) Sterilization of milk (b) Dehydration of milk (c) Fermentation of milk (d) Distillation of milk M.P. PCS (Pre) 2016 Ans. (a) The Pasteurization is a process that kills microbes (mainly bacteria) in food and drinks such as milk and facilitates its preservation and safety. In this process, the milk is heated at about 630 C for 30 minutes or, alternatively, at about 720 C for 15 seconds to ensure that any harmful bacteria is not alive. The process was invented by the French scientist Louis Pasteur. So it is called Pasteurization. 9. Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
